correctness.rationale: Neighborhood capacities give the odd lower bound and exclude k tokens on L_{2k}: equality would forbid overlap and endpoint tokens, forcing both second-column vertices to be selected and hence overlap. The alternating odd word and the displayed even words attain the respective bounds. For a minimum word the total excess coverage is 4|S|−e(S)−2n; 00 forces X00X, which consumes four excess incidences and is impossible in the odd case. In the even case those two X columns dominate the whole interval from one column before to one after the block. A token just outside that interval would create overlap, and dominating its column without such a token requires a third X; no such extension is possible. Endpoint selections are also forbidden in this case, leaving precisely 0X00X0 on L₆. Otherwise the empty/occupied count permits at most one X. On even ladders with no X both endpoints are occupied and the single missing internal zero specifies the gap, with independent alternating row phases on its two sides. With one X exactly one endpoint is empty, forcing the adjacent X and the other alternating singletons; these are the four endpoint-double words. For odd n≥5 a sole X would have to dominate both empty endpoints from two distinct columns, so there are just the two alternating words and no slide between them. For even n, moving the gap more than one position changes at least two occupied columns; when it moves one position, the moving token must keep its row, forcing s=r⊕(j mod 2). Rung moves can change a whole alternating block only when its length is one. The only slides to endpoint-double words are the indicated slides out of that endpoint, and two different endpoint-double words are not one move apart for k≥3. These checks give exactly the two B_{k−1} components and the asserted counts, diameter, and isolates. They also apply to the nonexceptional words at k=3. The exceptional word is frozen: every rung target is occupied, a move outward from an X loses one row of the inner empty column, and a move inward loses one row in the outer empty column. Independent finite replay for L₆: enumerate all subsets of the 12 vertices by size through 4, retain those whose closed-neighborhood union is the whole ladder, and test each replacement along a rung or rail. It gives minimum size 4, 17 vertices, 12 edges, component orders 7,7,1,1,1, and each 7-vertex tree has degrees 1⁴,2,3². The uploaded scripts were inspected, not run; the infinite result follows from the word and edge argument.

evidence: Anusuya–Kala Theorem 2.11 describes the connected modified γ_m graph for all n=2k, k≥4. Its labeled proof gives minimum-set families and lists four triangles and four paths. The bound's graph instead has isolates and two trees.
The inspected later Resultary entry concerns independent dominating sets. Its minimum even case is 2P_{n/2}; it excludes nonindependent minima and does not describe the full minimum-domination graph.
The abstract of Some Results on Gamma Graphs identifies path products but specifies an unrestricted exchange convention. Its actual ladder theorem is unverified.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A general adjacent-swap definition does not give an all-k classification. The unrestricted graph is a supergraph on the same minimum sets; its connectedness or degree distribution does not determine the structure of the edge-restricted graph. Restricting the vertex set to independent minima is not extension to all minima.

evidence: The prior labeled candidate exchanges substantially reduce the vertex and candidate-edge work. They do not classify which path families implement same-row slides and which change row while shifting columns. At a gap shift, the matching phase r⊕j is needed; at endpoint triangles the admissible pairs depend on a rung or a same-row rail rather than a diagonal exchange.
The two independent even-ladder paths account for the spine types, but by definition cannot account for nonindependent leaves or isolated minima.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new structural step is the uniform edge filter and proof of how the surviving path and triangle edges meet. The unrestricted graph considered as an abstract graph has no edge-type information; even using its labeled families one must establish the gap-phase condition along entire paths and check the endpoint cases. The broom/isolates theorem is not a specialization of the stated unrestricted degree or connectedness theorem.

evidence: Anusuya–Kala distinguish ordinary γ-graph adjacency, requiring v∼w, from modified γ_m adjacency, requiring only a one-vertex exchange. The bound uses the ordinary convention, not the modified one.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Terminology is not enough to distinguish results: the standard ordinary γ-graph is exactly the bound model and must count as a possible duplicate, whereas unrestricted exchange and a middle-graph construction are not equivalent. originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge credit is for the uniform, adjacency-constrained double-broom and isolate classification on ordinary even ladders, not for the general γ-graph model, domination number, enumeration of optima, or an unrelated graph on the same optima. The strongest accessible prior ladder graph is a labeled unrestricted-exchange graph with substantial overlap in the word families and candidate exchanges. Its stated parameters and topology are different; the surviving adjacent edges and resulting disconnected components need their own row-compatibility argument. The alternate graph conventions and source access limits below constrain this judgment.
residual_risks: The Fricke et al. primary full text and the Bhatt Cartesian-product article's full text were not available through the tried routes. Exact ladder coverage under the adjacent convention could exist in the former or another uninspected source.

The bibliographic description of Lakshmanan–Vijayakumar's edge convention was not independently verified. Conclusions about the modified graph follow the explicit definition in the accessible 2020 primary article, not a blanket assertion about γ-graph terminology.

value.rationale: The ordinary adjacent-swap γ-graph is a pre-existing natural object. For the simplest nontrivial ladder family, the theorem explains exactly which optimal selections are frozen and why the movable ones split into two trees of specified shape. This is a structural answer that the convenient count 4k+4 or the connected unrestricted graph does not provide. The main value is the uniform even-ladder classification and explicit obstruction mechanism; the finite L₆ check alone would not suffice.
